items.stimulus: Astronomers monitoring the young star HD 31460 noticed that its light dipped irregularly, sometimes by a fifth, for days at a time. items.stem: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
choices: It presents an observation of HD 31460 that allowed the team to rule out a planet as the cause of the dips.
It offers a general contrast explaining why the cause the team proposes fits the uneven dips better than a planet.
It states the team's conclusion that the planetary system around HD 31460 is still in the process of forming.
It raises a possible objection to the team's proposal that orbiting debris is responsible for the dips.
items.explanation: The underlined sentence names no star, date, or measurement. It states a general property of dust clouds. 'Therefore' in the next sentence shows that the team's proposal rests on this contrast.

items.stimulus: Fossil leaves are widely used to estimate ancient carbon dioxide levels, because many plants grow fewer stomata, or breathing pores, when the gas is plentiful. Paleobotanist Rhea Okafor asked whether this response holds for ferns, whose fossils are abundant in rocks too old for other methods. Growing twelve living fern species under varied carbon dioxide levels, she found that nine grew fewer stomata as levels rose. <u>The other three showed no consistent change, and all three belong to a lineage that grows in deep shade.</u> Okafor suggests that fern fossils can serve as gauges, provided their lineage is identified first.
items.stem: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
choices: It reports results that undermine Okafor's claim that ferns respond to carbon dioxide as other plants do.
It identifies a pattern among exceptions to the main finding that accounts for Okafor's stated condition.
It describes how Okafor chose which fern species to grow under the varied levels of carbon dioxide.
It explains why many plants grow fewer stomata when carbon dioxide is plentiful in the surrounding air.
items.explanation: The sentence before gives the main result: nine of twelve species responded. The underlined sentence covers the three that did not and notes what they share, a single shade-dwelling lineage. That shared trait is why Okafor's final suggestion comes with a condition: identify the lineage first. The sentence qualifies the finding. It does not overturn it.

items.stimulus: After the Varne River was dammed in 1974, wells in the downstream farming town of Elsby began to fall, and residents blamed the reservoir for holding back water that once soaked into the ground. <u>Records show that well levels dropped fastest in the decade the dam was completed.</u> Hydrologist Tomas Reyes, however, notes that the same decade saw Elsby's farms triple their pumping to water newly planted orchards, and that wells upstream of the dam, beyond the reservoir's reach, fell just as quickly.
items.stem: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
choices: It presents a pattern in timing that seems to back the residents' view but that Reyes shows fits another cause.
It provides the evidence that Reyes uses to show that the reservoir lowered the water table near Elsby.
It introduces Reyes's claim that increased pumping, rather than the dam, caused Elsby's wells to fall.
It establishes that the dam had no effect on groundwater levels anywhere along the Varne River.
items.explanation: The underlined sentence comes before 'however.' At that point, the decline lining up with the dam seems to support the residents. Reyes then points to a second change in the same decade, tripled pumping, and to upstream wells that fell just as fast. That shows the timing fits pumping equally well. The sentence sets up an apparent story that the rest of the text reframes.

B.why: You recognized the sentence as evidence but gave it to the wrong side. Reyes uses it to show that the timing points to more than one cause, not to blame the reservoir.

C.why: You pointed to the wrong part of the text. Reyes's alternative appears only after 'however.' The underlined sentence still belongs to the residents' account.

D.why: You took Reyes's doubt about the residents' explanation and made it absolute. Neither the sentence nor Reyes says the dam had no effect anywhere.

items.stimulus: Folklorists long treated the many versions of a folktale as corruptions of a lost original, ranking each by how faithfully it seemed to preserve that source. Scholar Aino Reinikainen argues instead that tellers reshape tales on purpose to suit their listeners. <u>In fishing villages along the Gulf of Bothnia, the tale of the clever youngest daughter ends with her outwitting a sea spirit; told inland, the same tale gives that role to a forest troll.</u> Such shifts, she contends, follow the local landscape too closely to be lapses of memory.
items.stem: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?

It describes the method earlier folklorists used to rank versions of a tale by their faithfulness to a source.
It shows that the tale of the clever youngest daughter first arose in the fishing villages of the Gulf of Bothnia.
items.explanation: The text sets up an old view (variants are corruptions) and then Reinikainen's view (variants are deliberate). The underlined sentence gives a concrete pair of variants. items.stimulus: When app-based delivery companies spread to midsize US cities, many observers predicted that restaurant kitchen workers would leave for the flexible new jobs, leaving restaurants short-staffed. items.stem: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
choices: It reports a finding that identifies the actual effect on restaurants in place of the effect observers predicted.
It qualifies the preceding finding by indicating that kitchen employment did fall in some of the cities.
It presents evidence supporting the observers' prediction that restaurants would be left short-staffed.
It explains the method Whitlock used to measure kitchen employment across the 140 cities she studied.
items.explanation: Observers predicted fewer kitchen workers, and the sentence before shows that did not happen. It replaces the predicted effect with the one actually observed.

items.stimulus: Can small earthquakes warn of large ones? Foreshocks precede some major quakes, but they look like ordinary tremors until afterward. Seismologist Keiko Mori studied a different signal: tiny repeating quakes that strike the same patch of a fault at steady intervals. <u>In the two years before a magnitude 7.1 quake struck off the Kaminari coast, the intervals between those repeating quakes shrank by half.</u> Mori cautions that a single record cannot show the pattern is reliable, but she argues that repeating quakes deserve monitoring in a way ordinary foreshocks do not.
items.stem: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
choices: It presents a finding that Mori treats as a reason for monitoring rather than as proof of a reliable warning sign.
It provides evidence that shrinking intervals reliably signal the approach of a major offshore earthquake.
It describes a foreshock pattern that, like other foreshocks, could be recognized only after the quake struck.
It explains how Mori identified the repeating quakes that struck the same patch of the fault at steady intervals.
items.explanation: The text opens with a question and introduces a new candidate signal. The underlined sentence gives a single result that looks promising. The next sentence sets limits on it: one record cannot show reliability, though it justifies monitoring. Getting this right means seeing both that the sentence supports Mori and that she limits how far it goes.

items.stimulus: Farmers plant cover crops such as rye after harvest to protect the soil, and many assume the rye also raises the next crop's yield. Field trials have been mixed: in some, corn planted after rye outyielded corn on bare soil; in others, it did worse. Agronomist Priya Nandakumar noticed that the trials differed in spring rainfall. <u>Rye roots open channels that drain water deep into the soil, but the living rye also pulls moisture out before it is cut down.</u> Where spring rain was heavy, the drainage helped the corn; where rain was scant, the lost moisture hurt it.
items.stem: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
choices: It describes two opposing effects of rye that together account for the conflicting results of the trials.
It presents evidence confirming farmers' assumption that rye raises the yield of the following corn crop.
It reports the results of Nandakumar's trials comparing corn grown after rye with corn on bare soil.
It explains why the amount of spring rainfall differed among the field trials Nandakumar reviewed.
items.explanation: The text starts with a puzzle: trials disagree. Nandakumar's clue is rainfall. The underlined sentence gives the mechanism, one effect that helps (drainage) and one that hurts (lost moisture). The final sentence shows that rainfall decides which effect wins, which resolves the conflicting results.

B.why: You focused on the helpful effect and missed the 'but.' Rye can also hurt yields, so the sentence explains the mixed results instead of confirming the farmers' assumption.

C.why: You called an explanation a result. The trial outcomes are given in the second sentence, and Nandakumar reviewed those trials rather than running them. The underlined sentence explains why the outcomes differed.

D.why: You linked 'water' in the sentence to the rainfall differences. The sentence explains how rye responds to water. It never says why rainfall varied among the trials.
